interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology demonstrated a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological T2 stage with no extraprostatic extension. Reassuring findings include negative surgical margins and no invasion of the seminal vesicles, as noted in the surgical pathology report: "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pathological stage pT2. There was no extraprostatic extension; surgical margins were negative; the seminal vesicles were not invaded." The absence of documented lymph node removal and nodal sampling means that the status is pNx, which does not establish node-negative disease. This missing nodal sampling widens the uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Countervailing findings are limited as no adverse nodal status or lymphovascular invasion was documented. The prognosis is significantly influenced by the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, which are currently unknown. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its trend is crucial for assessing biochemical recurrence risk. The fixed estimated horizon is 70.80 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 46.02–95.58 months; its coverage has not been validated.
